name: NJ-12
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strongly Democratic district (D+13 PVI) in a favorable national environment
Massive Democratic fundraising and outside-spending advantage over a barely funded Republican
Open seat removes incumbent advantage but does not change the partisan baseline
No polling or expert ratings, so forecast rests on fundamentals
model.rationale: The baseline model points to a ~21-point Democratic margin, and nothing in the evidence justifies moving: Hamawy outraised Mele roughly 19-to-1 with heavy outside support, while Mele has almost no cash. Polymarket prices the Democrat at 97%, consistent with a Safe D rating despite the open seat.
model.watch: A late surge of Republican outside spending or an unexpected Democratic primary fallout could narrow the margin, though a genuine upset remains very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Bonnie Watson Coleman (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
New Jersey's 12th District is a solidly Democratic seat, with a partisan lean of about 13 points toward Democrats and an open-seat baseline near 21 points once the favorable national environment is included. Incumbent Bonnie Watson Coleman is retiring, but the seat's fundamentals remain strongly favorable to the party holding it.

On the Democratic side, Adam Hamawy has raised about $1.5 million and benefits from nearly $2 million in outside support, while Republican Gregg Mele has raised under $80,000 with negligible cash on hand and no outside spending. There are no public polls or expert ratings, but prediction markets put the Democratic win probability around 97%. The forecast is Safe Democratic with a margin near 21 points and above-average uncertainty given the absence of polling.
